title: Missing colon after def/if/for/while/class
content: Python requires a colon at the end of compound statement headers: def, class, if, elif, else, for, while, try, except, with. Forgetting it raises 'SyntaxError: expected ':''. Fix: add ':' at the end of the header line, then indent the body. Example: write 'def add(a, b):' not 'def add(a, b)'.

title: IndentationError: expected an indented block / unexpected indent
content: Python uses indentation to define blocks. 'IndentationError: expected an indented block' means a header line (def, if, for...) has no indented body. 'unexpected indent' means a line is indented more than the block allows. Use 4 spaces consistently and never mix tabs and spaces (TabError). Configure the editor to insert spaces when Tab is pressed.

title: Unmatched parentheses, brackets or quotes
content: 'SyntaxError: '(' was never closed' or 'unterminated string literal' means brackets or quotes are not paired. Count opening and closing ( [ { and make sure every string starts and ends with the same quote type. The reported line is often the line AFTER the real mistake, so also inspect the line above.

title: Assignment (=) used instead of comparison (==) in a condition
content: In Python, 'if x = 5:' is a SyntaxError because '=' assigns while '==' compares. Use 'if x == 5:'. Python 3.8+ offers ':=' (walrus operator) only for intentional assignment expressions.

title: NameError: name is not defined
content: NameError occurs when a variable or function is used before it is defined, when it is misspelled, or when it was defined in a different scope (for example inside a function). Fix: define the variable before use, check spelling and capitalization (Python is case-sensitive), import the needed module, or return the value from the function.

title: TypeError: can only concatenate str (not 'int') to str
content: The + operator cannot join a string and a number. Convert explicitly: 'Age: ' + str(age), or use an f-string: f'Age: {age}'. Values read with input() are always strings, so convert with int() or float() before doing arithmetic.

title: IndexError: list index out of range
content: A list of length n has valid indexes 0 to n-1 (and -1 to -n). Accessing nums[len(nums)] or nums[5] on a 3-item list raises IndexError. Fix: check len() first, loop with 'for item in nums' or range(len(nums)), and remember indexing starts at 0.

title: KeyError and dictionary access
content: KeyError is raised when a key is missing from a dictionary. Use d.get(key, default), check 'if key in d', or catch KeyError. Keys are case-sensitive and types matter: 1 and '1' are different keys.

title: ValueError from int()/float() conversion
content: int('abc') or int('3.5') raises ValueError because the text is not a valid integer. Validate user input, wrap the conversion in try/except ValueError, or use float() first for decimal text. Strip whitespace with .strip().

title: ZeroDivisionError
content: Dividing or taking modulo by zero raises ZeroDivisionError. Check that the divisor is not zero before dividing, e.g. 'if b != 0:', or handle the error with try/except ZeroDivisionError.

title: Mutable default arguments and bare except
content: A default like def f(items=[]) is created once and shared across calls, causing surprising state. Use items=None and create a new list inside the function. A bare 'except:' hides real errors (even KeyboardInterrupt); catch specific exceptions such as 'except ValueError:'.

title: Infinite loop: loop variable never updated
content: A while loop runs forever if its condition never becomes false. Typical cause: forgetting to update the loop variable (i += 1 in Python, i++ in C/Java/JS) or updating it in the wrong direction. Fix: make sure every iteration moves the variable toward the stopping condition, and ensure 'while True' has a reachable break or return.

title: Off-by-one errors in loop bounds
content: Using <= instead of < (or range(n+1) instead of range(n)) makes the loop run one time too many and often causes an out-of-range array access. For an array of size n, valid indexes are 0..n-1, so the loop condition should be i < n. Check the first and last iteration by hand.

title: Incorrect conditions: = vs ==, wrong boolean operator
content: Common condition mistakes: using assignment instead of comparison (C/Java/JS: if (x = 5) assigns 5 and is always true), mixing && / || (and/or), writing a chained check wrongly (x > 1 and < 10 must be x > 1 and x < 10), and forgetting braces so only the first statement belongs to the if. Re-read the condition with real values to test it.

title: Condition ordering in if/elif/else chains
content: In an if/else-if chain, the first true branch wins. Put the most specific condition first (e.g. check score >= 90 before score >= 80). Otherwise broader conditions capture values and later branches are never executed.

title: Function argument count mismatch
content: Calling a function with too few or too many arguments is an error: Python raises 'TypeError: area() missing 1 required positional argument' and C/Java report compile errors. Match the call to the definition: same number, order and types of arguments, or give parameters default values.

title: Recursion without a base case or with a non-shrinking input
content: Every recursive function needs a base case that stops recursion and a recursive step that moves toward it. Missing base case leads to RecursionError (Python) or StackOverflowError (Java) or a segmentation fault (C). Example: factorial(n) must return 1 when n <= 1 and call factorial(n-1), not factorial(n).

title: Missing return value / return in the wrong place
content: A function without a return statement returns None in Python (undefined in JS). A return placed inside a loop's first iteration ends the function too early. In C/Java a non-void function must return a value on every path. Print is not the same as return.

title: Variable scope mistakes
content: Variables created inside a function are local to it. Using them outside raises NameError (Python) or is undeclared (C/Java). Return values or pass parameters rather than relying on globals. In Python assigning to a global inside a function needs the 'global' keyword.

title: Array index out of bounds
content: Arrays are zero-indexed. Accessing index n of an array with n elements is out of bounds: Java throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException, Python raises IndexError, JavaScript returns undefined, and C has undefined behaviour (it may silently corrupt memory). Always keep indexes in 0..length-1.

title: String immutability and comparison
content: Strings are immutable in Python, Java and JavaScript: s[0] = 'x' fails in Python, and methods like replace() return a NEW string that must be assigned. Compare string content with == in Python/JS, with .equals() in Java, and strcmp() in C.

title: Off-by-one when slicing or taking substrings
content: Python slices s[a:b] exclude index b. Java substring(a, b) also excludes b. A full copy of an n-length string is s[0:n], not s[0:n-1]. Check both ends with a short example.

title: Integer division and type conversion surprises
content: In C and Java, 5/2 is 2 because both operands are integers; cast one to double (5/2.0) to get 2.5. Python 3 '/' gives a float and '//' gives integer division. Convert input text to numbers explicitly: int(), float(), Integer.parseInt(), atoi().

title: Mixing incompatible types
content: Assigning a string to an int variable (Java: int x = "5";) or adding string and number in Python are type errors. Statically typed languages catch these at compile time; Python and JavaScript catch them at runtime or silently coerce. Convert explicitly and keep variable types consistent.

title: Missing semicolon and unbalanced braces
content: Every Java statement ends with ';'. Compiler messages like "';' expected" point at or just after the line with the problem. 'reached end of file while parsing' means a closing brace '}' is missing. Match every { with a }, and use an IDE that highlights matching braces.

title: Comparing Strings with == instead of .equals()
content: In Java == compares object references, not text. Two equal strings may compare false. Use s1.equals(s2) or s1.equalsIgnoreCase(s2). Put the literal first ('yes'.equals(input)) to avoid NullPointerException.

title: NullPointerException and uninitialised objects
content: NullPointerException occurs when calling a method or accessing a field on a reference that is null. Initialise objects with new, check for null before use, and remember arrays of objects start filled with null. Read the stack trace: the first line in your own code shows where.

title: Common compile errors: 'cannot find symbol' and incompatible types
content: 'cannot find symbol' means a variable, method or class name is misspelled, undeclared or not imported. Java is case-sensitive: System.out.println (capital S) not system.out.println. 'incompatible types' appears when assigning e.g. a double to an int without a cast or a String to an int.

title: scanf missing & address-of operator
content: scanf needs the ADDRESS of the variable to store input: scanf("%d", &n); not scanf("%d", n);. Without & the program writes to a garbage address and usually crashes. Character arrays (strings) are the exception: scanf("%s", name) needs no &.

title: Array out of bounds and buffer overflow
content: C does not check array bounds. Writing arr[5] in int arr[5] corrupts neighbouring memory and may crash later. Loop with i < size, not i <= size. Avoid gets() (removed in C11); use fgets(buf, sizeof buf, stdin) so input cannot overflow the buffer.

title: Missing #include and implicit declaration warnings
content: printf/scanf need #include <stdio.h>; strlen/strcpy need <string.h>; malloc/free need <stdlib.h>. Forgetting the header gives 'implicit declaration of function' warnings and can cause wrong behaviour.

title: Uninitialised variables and wrong printf format specifiers
content: Local variables in C are not initialised; reading them gives garbage. Initialise at declaration (int sum = 0;). The printf format must match the type: %d int, %f float/double (%lf for scanf double), %c char, %s string, %ld long. A mismatch prints wrong values.

title: Pointers: dangling, NULL dereference and memory leaks
content: Dereferencing NULL or a freed pointer crashes (segmentation fault). Check malloc's return value, set pointers to NULL after free(), and free() every malloc(). Use sizeof on the right type when allocating arrays.

title: == vs === and type coercion
content: == converts types before comparing (0 == '0' is true, '' == 0 is true) which causes surprising bugs. Use === and !== for strict comparison. Remember typeof null is 'object' and NaN !== NaN (use Number.isNaN).

title: TypeError: Assignment to constant variable (const)
content: Variables declared with const cannot be reassigned: const x = 1; x = 2; throws TypeError. Use let for values that change. Note const objects/arrays can still be mutated (push, property change) but not rebound.

title: undefined, ReferenceError and var hoisting
content: ReferenceError: x is not defined means the name does not exist in scope. Accessing a missing property or an array index out of range gives undefined, and calling a method on undefined throws TypeError. var is function-scoped and hoisted; prefer let/const which are block-scoped.

title: Assignment in conditions and async mistakes
content: if (x = 5) assigns 5 to x and is always truthy; use ===. For asynchronous code, forgetting await on a Promise returns the Promise object, not its value; and callbacks inside loops using var all see the final loop value, so use let.
